_comment: Single source of truth for cadence, format mix and posting slots. Read at runtime by generate_all_content.py, schedule_all_posts.cjs, send_to_slack.py, build_carousel_today.cjs and cap_infographic_today.js. Do not re-declare these values anywhere else.

llm._comment: Provider config for the content generator. base_url, model and api_key_env are the only places these are declared; change provider or model here, never in code. api_key_env names the .env variable holding the key - the value is never read into config, logged or printed.

adspy._comment: Where the ad-teardown pool is topped up from. The pipeline NEVER calls this at run time - it only reads sources/ad_teardowns/*.json. add_teardown.py starts this server if it is not already listening. 127.0.0.1 rather than localhost: on some setups localhost resolves to ::1 first and the server binds IPv4 only.

_rationale: Cut from ~3.7 posts/day to 1/weekday. Median was 51 impressions/post with ~half of posts getting zero engagement; posts were competing with each other.
polls cut: 8 polls produced 9 reactions and 2 comments total - high impressions, almost no engagement.
infographics cut: lowest-reach format in the account's own data.
document carousels kept: strongest performing format.
A count of 0 makes a format unused, not unavailable. Its code path is intact and returns immediately.

generate_performance_posts=false: the 5 report-driven posts were generated every run, written to performance_posts_<date>.txt, and read by nothing. They cost ~40% of the run and a single failure could abort the whole batch after topics were burned. The block is intact behind this flag, not deleted.

Phase 3: pillars replace 'whatever Reddit surfaced'. Audience was 18% IT services and 15% advertising - peers, not buyers - which followed directly from sourcing topics out of practitioner subreddits.
source_max_age_days=14: anything fed to the planner as current carries its own date and is refused past this. Two weeks is the point where a platform changelog stops being an update.
Pillar and format are independent axes. A pillar is a SOURCE; the format comes from format_mix. Each source item declares which formats it can carry and the resolver fails loudly if none matches.

reddit_per_sub_limit=25, reddit_delay_seconds=8: the community pillar uses exactly ONE question per run. Fetching 150 items to use 1, while getting 429-ed on r/facebookads, was the wrong trade. 429s now back off 30s/60s/90s rather than 4s.
_rules: with weekdays_only, a 7-day window always contains exactly 5 weekdays
format_order must list every key present in format_mix
slots are filled day by day, in time_slots order, until posts_per_batch is reached
post sequence is a round-robin over format_order, skipping formats whose count is 0 or exhausted
every pillar.source must be a source the resolver knows
a pillar that yields nothing aborts the run - it never silently swaps to another pillar
